topic: Leaky-IV tangent-contact inference in Watson et al.'s p=2 linear SEM. Let delta=tau^2-tau_check^2 approach zero over explicit local triangular arrays. Define the total positive-part plug-in interval on empirically infeasible samples, derive its exact square-root Gaussian endpoint law, derive the distinct data-dependent retained-resample kernel used by leakyIV, and prove ordinary/discarded bootstrap nonuniformity. Construct a multiplier score-inversion confidence hull with uniform whole-identified-set coverage, matched n^-1/4 minimax outer directed-Hausdorff loss at contact, root-n loss in the fixed interior, and adaptation by the same one-dimensional procedure. Use the explicit positive-definite Sigma(a) witness and exclude weak instruments by a fixed relevance bound. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: In the Gaussian witness, X=Z1+epsilon_x and Y=aZ2+epsilon_y imply sqrt(n)(delta_hat-delta_n) converges to N(0,4) along a_n^2=1-h/sqrt(n); after n^1/4 scaling the ordered endpoints become plus/minus sqrt((h+Z)_+). Conditional on the first-stage realization, retained bootstrap endpoints instead follow a random truncated kernel, establishing a concrete nonuniformity mechanism. A uniform score error r expands quadratic-contact sets by order sqrt(r) and interior sets by order r, so one root-n score hull plausibly adapts between n^-1/4 and n^-1/2. LAN contiguity along the witness supplies the converse route. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove one uniform multiplier approximation for the quadratic score process over both contact-local and interior classes that yields simultaneous whole-set coverage and expected outer-loss bounds under the same critical-value rule. EARLY KILL TEST: On the one-parameter Gaussian witness, prove uniformly for h in a fixed compact set that the score hull covers the entire interval with worst expected outer loss of order n^-1/4 and that the retained bootstrap has the stated random truncated kernel; pivot or stop if either assertion fails.

open_problems.open_problem: What are the joint contact-local law of the total positive-part plug-in endpoints and the conditional retained-resample endpoint kernel in Watson et al.'s fixed-relevance p=2 leaky-IV model, uniformly over delta_n=h/sqrt(n) for compact h?

source_refs.claim: The p=2 sharp bounds contain a square-root slack term, while Appendix A.9 argues differentiability and permits discarding infeasible bootstrap draws.
source_refs.author: David S. Watson, Jordan Penn, Lee M. Gunderson, Gecia Bravo-Hermsdorff, Afsaneh Mastouri, Ricardo Silva

source_refs.claim: The ordinary bootstrap can be inconsistent when the target is on the boundary of its parameter space.
source_refs.author: Donald W. K. Andrews

source_refs.claim: Full differentiability is necessary for standard-bootstrap consistency of nondegenerate Gaussian transforms, and derivative-based resampling can repair directional cases.
source_refs.author: Zheng Fang and Andres Santos

source_refs.excerpt: The bootstrap conditions on a random contact gap rather than on the population gap.
If retaining a negative result, target a named published intersection-bound implementation and quote the exact step.
Zero first stages, tangencies, shrinking gaps, exchange ties, singleton or zero-width sets are excluded.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Watson et al. treat the endpoint optimizer as smooth after conditioning on feasibility, but at delta=0 the explicit p=2 formula composes a root-n covariance slack with x -> sqrt(x_+), which is only one-half Hölder. Discarding infeasible resamples then conditions on a sample-dependent event with nondegenerate contact-local probability. The prior intersection-bound angle identified this random-gap mechanism but lacked a named workflow, while the BudgetIV work explicitly excluded tangencies and collapsed sets. The first missing proof step is an exact quadratic-root continuous-mapping calculation for a totalized random interval, followed by conditional analysis after feasibility selection.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A triangular-array theorem showing that the n^(1/4)-scaled ordered totalized endpoints converge to (-sqrt((h+Z)_+),sqrt((h+Z)_+)) under the positive-definite Gaussian Sigma(a) witness, deriving an explicit random conditional kernel for retained resamples, and proving a compact-h positive lower bound on ordinary and discarded bootstrap approximation error.

writing_exemplar.why: Mirror its progression from imperfect exclusion to sharp p=2 bounds and practical endpoint bootstrapping, then isolate contact as the point where its smoothness argument breaks.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Exclusion leakage makes the ATE set-identified -> the p=2 model supplies explicit sharp endpoints -> empirical feasibility can bind at equality -> square-root contact changes both endpoint and retained-bootstrap laws

method_exemplars.technique: Rewrite the closed-form p=2 L2 bounds using their scalar feasibility slack and expand that exact sharp-set map.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the precise identified interval whose totalized endpoint and resample laws must be characterized.

method_exemplars.technique: Separate the regular Gaussian primitive from its nonsmooth transform and compare the conditional bootstrap law with the fixed target law.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The leaky-IV interval is a nonsmooth transform of a regular covariance score, although its square-root map requires a slower scale than their Lipschitz directional framework.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the local boundary-sequence and conditional-bootstrap comparison used to establish bootstrap inconsistency.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Feasibility retention is an endogenous boundary event, making boundary-local bootstrap analysis the closest prototype for its random kernel.

open_problems.open_problem: Can one one-dimensional multiplier inversion of the p=2 leaky-IV quadratic feasibility score uniformly cover the whole identified interval while adapting from n^-1/4 expected outer directed-Hausdorff loss at contact to root-n loss in the fixed interior?

source_refs.claim: Watson et al. give sharp covariance-oracle ATE bounds and an endpoint bootstrap but no contact-uniform whole-set coverage theorem.
source_refs.author: David S. Watson, Jordan Penn, Lee M. Gunderson, Gecia Bravo-Hermsdorff, Afsaneh Mastouri, Ricardo Silva

source_refs.claim: Criterion or test inversion can construct random regions that uniformly cover an entire identified set.
source_refs.author: Joseph P. Romano and Azeem M. Shaikh

source_refs.claim: Bootstrap approximation of an estimated local parameter space yields uniformly valid inference in constrained identified and partially identified models.
source_refs.author: Victor Chernozhukov, Whitney K. Newey and Andres Santos

source_refs.excerpt: No theorem supplies the tie-uniform bootstrap approximation and inversion argument required for those guarantees.
The population Gaussianization theorem does not establish observable common-multiplier quantile consistency.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing identified-set inversion results control regular criterion or score processes, but here a root-n score error expands a quadratic-contact set by its square root while expanding an interior set linearly. The adjacent CausalSmith runs expose the same missing bridge: population Gaussian limits do not imply observable common-multiplier quantile validity uniformly through degeneracy. The required new step is one conditional multiplier coupling over contact-local and fixed-interior classes, combined with a deterministic score-error-to-set lemma whose modulus automatically changes from sqrt(r) to r without changing the statistic or critical-value rule.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A theorem for a single hull C_n obtained by inverting a multiplier-calibrated standardized leakage-feasibility score, proving uniform whole-identified-set coverage and expected outer directed-Hausdorff bounds O(n^-1/4) on delta_n=O(n^-1/2) arrays and O(n^-1/2) on fixed-interior laws under one fixed relevance bound.

writing_exemplar.why: Keep its applied object and covariance-level p=2 formulation while replacing endpoint resampling with a coverage-first inversion problem.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Leaky instruments yield a sharp ATE interval -> empirical work needs uncertainty for the entire interval -> endpoint bootstrapping becomes nonregular at feasibility contact -> invert the primitive score before applying the square-root endpoint map

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt their bootstrap coupling of an estimated local parameter space and inversion of constrained moment criteria, establishing uniform validity before mapping to the target set.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides a uniform resampling-and-inversion architecture for inequality-constrained partially identified models.

method_exemplars.technique: Use Gaussian multiplier coupling and anti-concentration for suprema of empirical scores to calibrate one simultaneous critical value.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The hull requires conditional approximation of a score process uniformly over candidate effect values.

method_exemplars.technique: Prove that inversion of the scalar quadratic feasibility inequality reproduces the paper's sharp p=2 L2 identified interval.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This connects the proposed score hull to the exact population identified set rather than to an outer relaxation.

open_problems.open_problem: Is n^-1/4 the local minimax expected outer directed-Hausdorff rate for honest estimation of Watson et al.'s p=2 leaky-IV interval at quadratic contact, with root-n optimality on fixed-interior subclasses?

source_refs.claim: The p=2 L2 sharp interval has endpoint displacement proportional to the square root of its nonnegative feasibility slack.
source_refs.author: David S. Watson, Jordan Penn, Lee M. Gunderson, Gecia Bravo-Hermsdorff, Afsaneh Mastouri, Ricardo Silva

source_refs.claim: Nondifferentiable bound functionals admit no locally asymptotically unbiased regular estimator, motivating local asymptotic minimax analysis.
source_refs.author: Keisuke Hirano and Jack R. Porter

source_refs.claim: A generalized van Trees inequality gives local minimax lower bounds for nonsmooth functionals and irregular models.
source_refs.author: Kenta Takatsu and Arun Kumar Kuchibhotla

open_problems.why_unsolved: The contact endpoint is a square root of a regular slack, so root-n-contiguous changes in the observable Gaussian SEM induce n^-1/4 changes in the identified set. Hirano and Porter establish an impossibility principle for nondifferentiable regular-rate bounds but do not give the fourth-root directed-Hausdorff constant, while generic set-estimation rates do not exploit the explicit positive-definite Sigma(a) LAN witness. The missing step is to transfer LAN contiguity through the square-root set map and compare risks under the same fixed-relevance restriction used for the attainable hull.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A Le Cam two-point, local-experiment, or generalized van Trees theorem on the Gaussian Sigma(a) submodel proving a positive compact-h lower bound for n^(1/4)-scaled worst expected outer directed-Hausdorff loss, plus matching hull upper bounds and an n^(1/2) upper-and-lower rate characterization in the fixed interior.

writing_exemplar.why: Mirror its progression from a concrete bounds functional through failure of regular estimation to an appropriate local-minimax criterion.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Bounds are nonsmooth functions of regular observables -> regular unbiased inference fails at the singularity -> local minimax risk becomes the relevant yardstick -> quantify the fourth-root price and adaptation frontier of leaky-IV contact

method_exemplars.technique: Specialize the generalized van Trees lower bound to the Gaussian covariance path and the set-valued square-root loss map, tracking its contact modulus.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its machinery targets nonsmooth functionals for which standard differentiable-functional efficiency bounds fail.

method_exemplars.technique: Use LAN paths and nondifferentiability to rule out regular endpoint estimators, then strengthen the comparison to directed-Hausdorff minimax risk.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It directly treats partially identified bounds that are nondifferentiable functions of regular statistical primitives.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt criterion-level-set estimation and its error-bound argument to prove the attainable outer-loss rate.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its geometric loss compares an estimated level set with an identified set, but the leaky-IV application requires a quadratic-contact growth modulus.

open_problems.open_problem: Can a numerical, m-out-of-n, or local-map bootstrap consistently estimate the contact-local leaky-IV endpoint law without discarding infeasible draws uniformly over unknown compact-h sequences, or is score inversion necessary?

source_refs.claim: The implemented leakyIV bootstrap discards resamples that violate partial identifiability and conditions inference on retained draws.
source_refs.author: David S. Watson, Jordan Penn, Lee M. Gunderson, Gecia Bravo-Hermsdorff, Afsaneh Mastouri, Ricardo Silva

source_refs.claim: The numerical bootstrap is valid for multiple nonregular problems and is analyzed under fixed and drifting parameter sequences.
source_refs.author: Han Hong and Jessie Li

source_refs.claim: At first-order degeneracy the standard second-order bootstrap generally fails, while corrected schemes can obtain local size control under additional conditions.
source_refs.author: Qihui Chen and Zheng Fang

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing corrections estimate directional derivatives or higher-order expansions, but the leaky-IV endpoint map x -> sqrt(x_+) has an unbounded derivative, a natural n^-1/4 scale, and an unknown local index h controlling both its atom and continuous component. The first proof step that must change is the derivative-estimation lemma: it must be replaced by a half-Hölder local-map approximation jointly with the root-n feasibility score. Searches pairing leakyIV with numerical bootstrap, m-out-of-n inference, and square-root positive-part IV bounds found no occupied target-method result.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Either a data-driven tuning theorem for a numerical or m-out-of-n bootstrap whose conditional endpoint law converges uniformly over compact h and yields valid whole-interval critical values, or an impossibility theorem for uniformly valid endpoint resampling that states conditions under which score inversion is necessary.

writing_exemplar.why: Frame the correction as a direct inferential replacement for the paper and package's retained bootstrap.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Sharp leaky-IV bounds are computable -> the package resamples their endpoints and removes infeasible draws -> contact makes retention informative and endpoint scaling nonregular -> determine whether a corrected endpoint-resampling workflow remains possible

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the inflated bootstrap perturbation and drifting-sequence approximation proof, replacing ordinary differentiation with the rescaled square-root positive-part local map.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is a direct resampling remedy with theory for nonregular rates and drifting parameters.

method_exemplars.technique: Separate primitive bootstrap validity from nonlinear-map failure and adapt the local-uniformity argument to half-Hölder contact.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The leaky-IV endpoint combines degeneracy and nonsmoothness, the mixed failure mode nearest to their framework.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over the bootstrap-of-an-estimated-local-map design and its differentiability-based necessity argument.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies both a constructive template and a route to impossibility if the endpoint's local map cannot be estimated uniformly.

open_problems.open_problem: Can the scalar quadratic-contact score-hull construction be extended to p>1 nested-quota BudgetIV envelopes with simultaneous endpoint tangencies and optimizer-exchange ties, with local strata determining sharp adaptive Hausdorff-loss rates?

source_refs.excerpt: Endpoint recovery requires unique active quota assignments and a uniform positive exchange-cycle margin.
Add a primitive regular-face assumption requiring positive component widths and gaps.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The prior BudgetIV construction relies on a fixed active quota assignment, separated components, and a positive exchange-cycle margin; all three fail when rational boundary pieces touch or an optimizer switches. The first changed proof step is to replace the p=2 scalar quadratic expansion by a tangent-cone expansion over every locally competitive quota assignment and exchange cycle, after which scalar score inversion becomes finite-envelope inversion. No prior-proposal artifact establishes coverage or rate adaptation on these singular strata.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A stratified local asymptotic theorem indexed by tangency order and active exchange-cycle multiplicity, together with a multiplier score-inversion confidence set attaining uniform whole-set coverage and the corresponding minimax expected directed-Hausdorff rate on each stratum.

writing_exemplar.why: Its nested invalidity budgets and quota geometry directly frame the destination problem.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Researchers permit graded numbers of invalid instruments -> nested budgets create quota-optimized identified sets -> optimizer ties and tangent endpoints invalidate regular-face inference -> characterize and infer across the resulting singular strata

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt uniformly calibrated projection over finite-dimensional moment equalities and inequalities to all locally competitive quota faces.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Each quota assignment generates a finite feasibility system, making calibrated projection natural once its local active envelope is characterized.

method_exemplars.technique: Combine directional differentiation of finite minima and maxima with corrected resampling of their Gaussian limits.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Exchange ties produce a finite min-max envelope, while tangency adds the slower square-root layer.

literature_map:
Watson et al. (2024, UAI, arXiv:2404.04446) derive sharp leaky-IV ATE bounds; for p=2 their endpoint radius contains a square root of the leakage slack.
Watson et al.'s Appendix A.9 asserts differentiability/bootstrap validity and permits discarding infeasible resamples, creating the central contact-level tension.
Conley, Hansen, and Rossi (2012, ReStat, doi:10.1162/REST_a_00139) are the foundational plausible-exogeneity anchor for relaxing exclusion restrictions.
Masten and Poirier (2021, Econometrica, arXiv:1812.11598) frame continuous IV-assumption relaxations through falsification frontiers and adaptive sets.
Penn et al. (2025, AISTATS, arXiv:2411.06913) extend the invalid-instrument program to budgeted violations and potentially disconnected feasible sets, but not p=2 tangent-contact inference.
Andrews (2000, Econometrica, doi:10.1111/1468-0262.00114) establishes ordinary-bootstrap inconsistency at parameter-space boundaries.
Fang and Santos (2019, ReStud, arXiv:1404.3763) characterize bootstrap validity for directionally differentiable transforms and develop derivative-based resampling.
Chen and Fang (2019, JoE, arXiv:1901.04861) isolate bootstrap failure under first-order degeneracy and provide modified remedies.
Hong and Li (2020, AoS, arXiv:1704.08066) develop a numerical bootstrap for nonregular rates and drifting sequences, but not the half-Hölder sqrt(x_+) contact map.
Chernozhukov, Hong, and Tamer (2007, Econometrica, doi:10.1111/j.1468-0262.2007.00794.x) establish criterion inversion, set-convergence rates, and confidence regions for parameter sets.
Romano and Shaikh (2010, Econometrica, doi:10.3982/ECTA6706) give uniformly valid regions covering whole identified sets.
Bugni (2010, Econometrica, doi:10.3982/ECTA8056) shows that the whole-set coverage target and binding moments matter for bootstrap inference.
Chernozhukov, Newey, and Santos (2023, Econometrica, arXiv:1509.06311) bootstrap estimated local parameter spaces for uniform constrained-moment inference.
Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato (2013, AoS, arXiv:1212.6906) supply Gaussian multiplier coupling and anti-concentration tools for simultaneous score control.
Hirano and Porter (2012, Econometrica, doi:10.3982/ECTA8681) motivate local-minimax analysis for nondifferentiable bounds; Takatsu and Kuchibhotla (2024, arXiv:2405.06437) provide modern nonsmooth lower-bound machinery.
